scores.evidence: The server writes it durably to Postgres before acknowledging it (synchronous), then broadcasts it to other users immediately.
scores.rationale: Claims about Yjs/CRDT behavior, fencing tokens, lease ownership, relative positions, and durability semantics are accurate and precise, including honest limits like CRDT metadata overhead triggers.

scores.evidence: A browser-based rich-text editor where many users edit the same document at once, see each other's cursors, and get version history
scores.rationale: Covers nearly every implied core need with explicit, justified deferrals, but collaborative per-user undo is never addressed, a core implied editor capability.

scores.evidence: Exactly one sync server owns each document at a time, via a lease in Redis with a fencing token so an old owner can't keep writing.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership, and the availability-vs-consistency split by data type are declared once and honored consistently across every phase with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Simulate 5+ clients making random concurrent edits under random network splits, delays and reorderings. Assert that all states end up byte-identical.
scores.rationale: Riskiest assumptions (convergence, durability, failover) are tested early with checkable exit criteria, chaos tests, and a production divergence detector that continues validation after launch.

scores.evidence: Or merge metadata exceeding about 3× the document's content size on typical documents after compaction.
scores.rationale: Every major decision states a default plus an explicit revisit trigger, numbers are hedged ('about'), and design-sensitive assumptions like server-readable content are flagged before lock-in.

scores.evidence: Divergence detector: clients periodically report a hash of their state. Mismatches raise a metric and a page-out alert.
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures: silent divergence, stale-owner split-brain, duplicate edits, malicious viewer writes, XSS, orphaned anchors, reconnect storms, each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Terraform builds the infrastructure. GitHub Actions builds the image, runs tests and database migrations, and does a rolling deploy to ECS
scores.rationale: Deployment, graceful drain, meaningful metrics, alerting and staging parity are concrete and team-sized, but deploy/migration rollback and incident ownership are not explicitly specified.

scores.evidence: Postgres full-text search first; OpenSearch is deferred.
scores.rationale: Money, compute and vendor costs are never discussed; cost awareness is only implicit in buy-vs-build and deferral choices, with no drivers, scaling behavior or estimates.

scores.evidence: This is effectively irreversible after Phase 1, because it changes storage, validation, search and export. Decide before the data format is locked.
scores.rationale: One-way doors (data format, encryption, tenancy) are identified, validated early, and isolated with explicit exit paths, while reversible choices get quick defaults with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith. One repo and one container image, run in three roles
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable design (monolith, Postgres-first, pg-boss, Hocuspocus scaffold) and defers microservices, OpenSearch and multi-region behind concrete pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: A signed-in user opens document /d/{id} and types "hello". A second user in another browser sees "hello" appear.
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: a concrete first slice, dependency-justified phase ordering, specific technology decisions, measurable exit checks per phase, and triggers for changing course.

checklist.evidence: CRDT (Yjs). It merges edits made offline or during a network split without a central sequencer.
a versioned ProseMirror schema (schema_version stamped on every document)... add-only node types, and unknown nodes are kept intact
Simulate 5+ clients making random concurrent edits under random network splits, delays and reorderings. Assert that all states end up byte-identical.
append-only doc_updates log plus periodic snapshots... A compaction job runs in the worker role.
Connections go to the owning server via consistent hashing on doc_id... Cap edit size and rate per connection.
The client keeps an offline queue in IndexedDB (y-indexeddb), and reconnects with backoff plus jitter.
Checks happen when a connection opens and on every incoming edit... A permission change disconnects affected sessions.
A restore is applied as a new forward edit, never a destructive rewrite.
Presence data (cursors, who's online) goes on a separate channel and is never stored.
Phase 1 — Document substrate: data format, storage, permissions, merge correctness... Unlocks: every feature that stores or changes document content.
500 concurrent editors on one document, and 50,000 documents open... Batch broadcasts for very busy documents.
An old client opening a document with new node types keeps the content intact; the client is gated on version and forced to refresh.

traps.evidence: Buy or adopt: Yjs, TipTap/ProseMirror... Scaffold: Hocuspocus as the first sync server.
Phase 0... A second user in another browser sees "hello" appear.
The server acknowledges only after the write commits.

note: An exceptionally strong, correctly sequenced CRDT-based plan with early convergence/durability validation and explicit reversibility reasoning; its only material gaps are the complete absence of cost treatment and no collaborative undo.
